summary: Luna Calumbo is a browser-based 3D mission trainer that lets young learners fly a first Angolan mission to the Moon. Players take the role of Kiala, a junior astronaut at GGPEN, Angola’s space programme office, and go through the whole journey: choosing the fuel load, launching, travelling to the Moon, deploying the ANGOSAT-2 satellite and landing. Before landing, a small scout robot is released from the ship. It analyses candidate landing zones (slope, boulders, soil strength, dust, sunlight, temperature, radiation and line-of-sight to Earth), sends notifications to the ship, and marks the safe zone with a beacon. Players then run a lunar outpost, balancing energy, oxygen, food and radiation through a solar storm. The project answers the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by turning real mission ideas (rocket equation, lunar gravity, landing-site selection, surface operations) into short playable lessons. It matters because it brings space education to students in Angola and Portuguese-speaking countries, in their own language, in any browser with no installation.
details:
What it does. Luna Calumbo is a set of short, playable missions. In the guided Journey, the player follows Kiala from Earth to the Moon: she puts on her suit, helps assemble the rocket, chooses a fuel load inside a valid window, launches, reaches lunar orbit, deploys the ANGOSAT-2 satellite and lands. In the trainer missions, the player lands manually under lunar gravity (1.62 m/s²), plans the mission with the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, and runs a lunar outpost with three levels, managing energy, oxygen, food and radiation, including a solar storm and simulated vital signs, ending with an educational report.

Scout robot. When the ship reaches lunar orbit it releases a small robot. The robot lands, drives to three candidate zones (rocky plateau, crater rim, smooth plain) and measures eight parameters in each: slope, boulder density, soil firmness, dust depth, sun elevation, ground temperature, radiation and Earth line-of-sight. Each result is sent to the ship as a notification. At the end the robot plants a beacon on the only safe zone and the ship lands next to it. This teaches why landing sites are chosen with data and not by chance.

Benefits and impact. It makes space careers concrete for children and teenagers in Angola, in Portuguese, with a local story (the Calumbo launch site, the Angolan flag, GGPEN, ANGOSAT-2). It runs in a normal browser with no installation and works offline. For classroom use the demo can be paused or run at 0.5×, 1× and 2× speed.

Tools. HTML, CSS and JavaScript; Three.js (r128) for 3D graphics; the Web Audio API for sound effects; a small PHP and file-based API for the ranking. All textures and models are generated by code.

Creativity. A national, culturally specific space story, a celebration with dance and music at the end of the mission, and a robot that “talks” to the ship, in place of a generic trainer.

Honest limits. Site conditions, illumination and robot measurements are simplified, simulated values for teaching and are labelled as such in the app. Delta-v values are Apollo-based references, and the energy model is simplified.
